blockMcqs.question: What is a container, fundamentally?
options: A lightweight VM with its own kernel
A host process isolated by namespaces and a cgroup
An emulator running a guest OS
A static binary with bundled libraries
blockMcqs.explanation: It runs natively on the host kernel; there is no guest OS or emulation inside.

blockMcqs.question: Which namespace lets two containers both bind port 8080?
blockMcqs.explanation: Each has its own interfaces and port space, so the ports never collide.

blockMcqs.question: What stops one container from consuming all the host's RAM?
blockMcqs.explanation: Namespaces only isolate the view; cgroups meter the resource budget.

blockMcqs.question: When a container modifies a file from a read-only layer, what happens?
options: The read-only layer is edited in place
The file is copied up to the writable layer first
A new image layer is committed
blockMcqs.explanation: Copy-on-write preserves the shared lower layers so other containers reuse them.

blockMcqs.question: Which component actually makes the namespace and cgroup syscalls?
blockMcqs.explanation: dockerd and containerd delegate the kernel-facing work to the minimal runc runtime.

blockMcqs.question: Why copy requirements.txt and install deps before copying app code?
options: It shrinks the final image size
pip requires it to run first
The slow deps layer stays cached across code changes
It avoids a separate writable layer
blockMcqs.explanation: Ordering least-to-most changing keeps the expensive layer out of frequent rebuilds.

blockMcqs.question: Why do containers boot far faster than VMs?
options: They share the host kernel, so there is no OS boot
blockMcqs.explanation: A VM must boot a full guest OS; a container is just a process starting natively.

blockMcqs.question: Why did Kubernetes dropping Docker not break existing images?
options: Docker images are a special incompatible format
K8s talks to any OCI runtime via the CRI
blockMcqs.explanation: Only the node-level shim changed; OCI images stay runtime-agnostic.

blockMcqs.question: A container exits with code 137. What most likely happened?
options: It received SIGTERM and stopped gracefully
The CPU limit throttled it to a halt
The OOM killer hit its memory limit
blockMcqs.explanation: 137 = 128 + 9 (SIGKILL); CPU limits throttle rather than kill.

blockMcqs.question: Where must data you want to survive a container restart live?
options: In a volume or bind mount
blockMcqs.explanation: The writable layer is destroyed with the container, taking its data with it.
